The '''63rd Academy Awards''' ceremony, organized by the [[Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences]] (AMPAS), took place on March 25, 1991, at the [[Shrine Auditorium]] in [[Los Angeles]] beginning at 6:00&nbsp;p.m. [[Pacific Time Zone|PST]] / 9:00&nbsp;p.m. [[Eastern Time Zone|EST]]. During the ceremony, [[Academy Awards]] (commonly referred to as the Oscars) were presented in 22 categories. The ceremony, which was televised in the United States on [[American Broadcasting Company|ABC]], was produced by [[Gilbert Cates|Gil Cates]] and directed by [[Jeff Margolis]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Credits |url=http://jeffmargolisproductions.com/credits/ |publisher=Jeff Margolis Productions |access-date=October 4, 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131005000932/http://jeffmargolisproductions.com/credits/ |archive-date=October 5, 2013 }}</ref> Actor [[Billy Crystal]] hosted for the second consecutive year.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Kleid |first1=Beth |title=Awards Update |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1991-01-24-ca-810-story.html |access-date=November 29, 2010 |work=Los Angeles Times |date=January 24, 1991 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714125925/http://articles.latimes.com/1991-01-24/entertainment/ca-810_1_academy-awards |archive-date=July 14, 2014 }}</ref> Three weeks earlier, in a ceremony held at [[The Beverly Hilton]] in [[Beverly Hills, California]] on March 2, the [[Academy Award for Technical Achievement|Academy Awards for Technical Achievement]] were presented by host [[Geena Davis]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Past Scientific & Technical Awards Ceremonies|url=http://www.oscars.org/awards/scitech/pastawards.html|access-date=July 31, 2013|publisher=[[Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140213185729/http://www.oscars.org/awards/scitech/pastawards.html|archive-date=February 13, 2014}}</ref>

''[[Dances With Wolves]]'' won seven awards, including [[Academy Award for Best Picture|Best Picture]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Rother |first1=Larry |title=Kevin Costner and 'Dances With Wolves' Win Top Oscar Prizes |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1991/03/26/movies/kevin-costner-and-dances-with-wolves-win-top-oscar-prizes.html |access-date=July 9, 2014 |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=March 26, 1991 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714133359/http://www.nytimes.com/1991/03/26/movies/kevin-costner-and-dances-with-wolves-win-top-oscar-prizes.html |archive-date=July 14, 2014 }}</ref> Other winners included ''[[Dick Tracy (1990 film)|Dick Tracy]]'' with three awards, ''[[Ghost (1990 film)|Ghost]]'' with two awards, and ''[[American Dream (film)|American Dream]]'', ''[[Creature Comforts]]'', ''[[Cyrano de Bergerac (1990 film)|Cyrano de Bergerac]]'', ''[[Days of Waiting: The Life & Art of Estelle Ishigo|Days of Waiting]]'', ''[[Goodfellas]]'', ''[[The Hunt for Red October (film)|The Hunt for Red October]]'', ''[[Journey of Hope (film)|Journey of Hope]]'', ''[[The Lunch Date]]'', ''[[Misery (film)|Misery]]'', ''[[Reversal of Fortune]]'', and ''[[Total Recall (1990 film)|Total Recall]]'' with one. The telecast garnered nearly 43 million viewers in the United States.

== Winners and nominees ==
<!-- Please do not add any fact or statement below unless you have a credible source verifying it. Otherwise, it will be promptly removed. -->

The nominees for the 63rd Academy Awards were announced on February 13, 1991, at 5:38&nbsp;a.m. [[Pacific Time Zone|PST]] (13:38 UTC) at the [[Samuel Goldwyn Theater]] in Beverly Hills, California, by [[Karl Malden]], president of the academy, and actor [[Denzel Washington]].<ref>{{harvnb|Wiley|Bona|1996|p=795}}</ref> ''[[Dances With Wolves]]'' led the nominations with twelve total; ''[[Dick Tracy (1990 film)|Dick Tracy]]'' and ''[[The Godfather Part III]]'' tied for second with seven each.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Fox |first1=David J |title=Oscar Dances With 'Wolves' : Costner Film Leads Pack With 12 Nominations |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1991-02-14-ca-1669-story.html |access-date=July 9, 2014 |work=Los Angeles Times |date=February 14, 1991 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714210148/http://articles.latimes.com/1991-02-14/entertainment/ca-1669_1_oscar-nominations |archive-date=July 14, 2014 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last1=Ryan |first1=Desmond |title=Oscar's Choices In The Academy Award Nominations, Kevin Costner's Epic, "Dances With Wolves," Did What No Movie Had Done Since "Reds" - Get A Dozen Nods. |url=http://articles.philly.com/1991-02-14/news/25772464_1_academy-award-nominations-category-of-best-actor-oscar |access-date=March 25, 2015 |work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]] |date=February 14, 1991 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150328090018/http://articles.philly.com/1991-02-14/news/25772464_1_academy-award-nominations-category-of-best-actor-oscar |archive-date=March 28, 2015 }}</ref>

The winners were announced during the awards ceremony on March 25, 1991.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Rickey |first1=Carrie |title=Kevin Costner's Night To Howl "Dances With Wolves" Takes Home Seven Oscars From 12 Nominations, While Kathy Bates And Jeremy Irons Take Top Acting Awards. |url=http://articles.philly.com/1991-03-26/news/25793365_1_oscar-ceremonies-sacheen-littlefeather-marlon-brando-s-oscar |access-date=February 25, 2015 |work=The Philadelphia Inquirer |date=March 26, 1991 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402182501/http://articles.philly.com/1991-03-26/news/25793365_1_oscar-ceremonies-sacheen-littlefeather-marlon-brando-s-oscar |archive-date=April 2, 2015 }}</ref> [[Kevin Costner]] became the fifth person to earn the Best Director Award for his directorial debut and to earn nominations for Best Actor and Best Director for the same film.<ref>{{cite news|last=Lyttelton |first=Oliver |title=Oscar Trivia: 50 Fun Facts To Prepare You For The 85th Academy Awards |url=http://blogs.indiewire.com/theplaylist/50-pieces-of-oscar-trivia-to-prepare-you-for-the-academy-awards-on-sunday-20130220?page=3 |access-date=July 5, 2013 |newspaper=[[IndieWire]] |publisher=[[Snagfilms]] |date=February 20, 2013 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130330181810/http://blogs.indiewire.com/theplaylist/50-pieces-of-oscar-trivia-to-prepare-you-for-the-academy-awards-on-sunday-20130220?page=3 |archive-date=March 30, 2013 }}</ref><ref>{{harvnb|Wiley|Bona|1996|p=1166}}</ref> Best Supporting Actress winner [[Whoopi Goldberg]] was the [[List of black Academy Award winners and nominees#Best Actress in a Supporting Role|second African American woman]] to win an award. [[Hattie McDaniel]] previously won in the same category for ''[[Gone with the Wind (film)|Gone With the Wind]]''.<ref name="PWBV">{{harvnb|Wiley|Bona|1996|p=798}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last1=Lewis |first1=Claude |title=Whopee for Whoopi Goldberg |url=http://articles.philly.com/1991-03-27/news/25789984_1_blacks-white-athletes-hattie-mcdaniel |access-date=July 9, 2014 |work=The Philadelphia Inquirer |date=March 27, 1991 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714213656/http://articles.philly.com/1991-03-27/news/25789984_1_blacks-white-athletes-hattie-mcdaniel |archive-date=July 14, 2014 }}</ref>

* ''[[Total Recall (1990 film)|Total Recall]]'' – [[Eric Brevig]], [[Rob Bottin]], [[Tim McGovern]] and [[Alex Funke]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Silver |first1=Edward |title=The Highs and Lows of Future Special Effects : Movies: Character-driven stories are dominating due to a recession mentality. But summer releases will pack plenty of visual ingenuity |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1991-03-25-ca-739-story.html |access-date=January 16, 2014 |work=Los Angeles Times |date=March 25, 1991 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714192823/http://articles.latimes.com/1991-03-25/entertainment/ca-739_1_effects-movie |archive-date=July 14, 2014 }}</ref>

===[[Academy Honorary Awards|Honorary Awards]]===
* To [[Sophia Loren]], one of the genuine treasures of world cinema who, in a career rich with memorable performances, has added permanent luster to our art form.<ref name="HonoraryOscars">{{harvnb|Kinn|Piazza|2002|p=269}}</ref>
* To [[Myrna Loy]], in recognition of her extraordinary qualities both on screen and off, with appreciation for a lifetime's worth of indelible performances.<ref name="HonoraryOscars" />

==Ceremony information==
[[File:Billy Crystal by Gage Skidmore.jpg|thumb|130px|right|[[Billy Crystal]] hosted the ceremony.|alt=Photo of Billy Crystal in 2018]]

Riding on the critical praise from [[62nd Academy Awards|last year's ceremony]], the academy rehired former film producer and former [[Directors Guild of America]] president [[Gilbert Cates]] to oversee production of the Oscar ceremony for the second straight time.<ref>{{cite news|title=Short Takes: Dates for '91 Oscars Scheduled |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1990-09-21-ca-956-story.html |access-date=February 27, 2011 |work=Los Angeles Times |date=September 21, 1990 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714122947/http://articles.latimes.com/1990-09-21/entertainment/ca-956_1_oscars-scheduled |archive-date=July 14, 2014 }}</ref> Two months before the awards gala, Cates selected actor and comedian [[Billy Crystal]] to host the show for the second consecutive year.<ref name="Orlando">{{cite news|title=Crystal Will Again Be Host Of Academy Awards Show |url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/1991/01/25/crystal-will-again-be-host-of-academy-awards-show/ |access-date=February 27, 2014 |work=Orlando Sentinel |date=January 25, 1991 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714164020/http://articles.orlandosentinel.com/1991-01-25/news/9101250672_1_academy-awards-show-crystal-shrine-auditorium |archive-date=July 14, 2014 }}</ref> Crystal made light of the honor by saying, "It's a great honor, and I hope to bring the show in under nine hours."<ref name="Orlando" />

As with last year's theme of "Around the World in 3 1/2 Hours," Cates centered the show around a theme. He christened the ceremony with the theme "100 Years of Film" in celebration of the centennial of the development of both the [[kinetoscope]] by [[Thomas Edison]] and celluloid film by [[Eastman Kodak]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Sloan|first1=Eugene|title=Movies Are the Star of the Show|work=USA Today |date=March 25, 1991|page=5D}}</ref> In tandem with the theme, the show featured an ambitious opening segment. Actor [[Michael Caine]] introduced the segment live via satellite from the [[Salon Indien du Grand Café]] in [[Paris]], where the short film ''[[L'Arrivée d'un train en gare de La Ciotat]]'' made its debut in 1895.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Scott|first1=Jay|title=Oscar awards|work=The Globe and Mail |date=March 26, 1991|page=C1}}</ref> After a brief clip of the film, the show cut back to the Shrine Auditorium stage, where actress [[Jasmine Guy]] and other dancers performed while a montage of film clips was projected in the background.<ref name="Wiley 1996 812">{{harvnb|Wiley|Bona|1996|p=812}}</ref> Filmmaker [[Chuck Workman]] filmed a vignette featuring actors such as [[Sally Field]], [[Andy García]], and [[Anjelica Huston]] discussing the first movie the actors watched.<ref>{{harvnb|Wiley|Bona|1996|p=806}}</ref>

Several other people participated in the production of the ceremony. Film composer and musician [[Bill Conti]] served as musical director for the ceremony.<ref>{{cite web|title=Events |url=http://www.billconti.org/works/events/ |publisher=Bill Conti |access-date=June 22, 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150109153751/http://www.billconti.org/works/events/ |archive-date=January 9, 2015 }}</ref> Dancer [[Debbie Allen]] choreographed a dance number showcasing the Best Original Score nominees.<ref>{{harvnb|Wiley|Bona|1996|p=805}}</ref> Despite losing eight members of her band in a plane crash, a visibly emotional [[Reba McEntire]] performed the Best Original Song nominee "I'm Checkin' Out" from the film ''[[Postcards from the Edge (film)|Postcards from the Edge]]''.<ref>{{cite news|last1=MacCambridge|first1=Michael|title=Wolves' leads the pack with seven awards|work=Austin American-Statesman |date=March 26, 1991|page=D1}}</ref> At the beginning of the ceremony, wrangler Lisa Brown escorted host Crystal, and Beechnut, a horse that was prominently featured in the upcoming film ''[[City Slickers]]''.<ref>{{harvnb|Wilson|2007|p=150}}</ref>

===Box office performance of nominees===
At the time of the nominations announcement on February 12, the combined gross of the five Best Picture nominees at the US box office was $458.2 million with an average of $41 million per film.<ref name=BoxOfficeOscars>{{cite news|title=1990 Academy Award Nominations and Winner for Best Picture |url=https://boxofficemojo.com/oscar/chart/?yr=1990&p=.htm |access-date=July 10, 2014 |work=[[Box Office Mojo]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140709002600/http://boxofficemojo.com/oscar/chart/?yr=1990&p=.htm |archive-date=July 9, 2014 }}</ref> ''Ghost'' was the highest earner among the Best Picture nominees, with $213.5 million in domestic box office receipts. The film was followed by ''Dances With Wolves'' ($104.3 million), ''The Godfather Part III'' ($62.5 million), ''Goodfellas'' ($41 million), and finally ''Awakenings'' ($36.7 million).<ref name=BoxOfficeOscars/>

Of the top 50 highest-grossing films released in 1990, 51 nominations went to 12 films on the list. Only ''Ghost'' (2nd), ''Pretty Woman'' (3rd), ''Dances With Wolves'' (8th), ''Dick Tracy'' (9th), ''The Godfather Part III'' (17th), ''Goodfellas'' (30th), and ''Awakenings'' (34th) were nominated for Best Picture, directing, acting, or screenwriting. The other top 50 box office hits that earned nominations were ''Home Alone'' (1st), ''The Hunt for Red October'' (5th), ''Total Recall'' (6th), ''Days of Thunder'' (12th), and ''Edward Scissorhands'' (22nd).<ref>{{cite news|title=1990 Box Office Grosses (as of February 12, 1991) |url=https://boxofficemojo.com/yearly/chart/?asof=1991-02-12&view=releasedate&view2=domestic&yr=1990&sort=gross&order=DESC&p=.htm |access-date=July 10, 2014 |work=Box Office Mojo |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714154754/http://boxofficemojo.com/yearly/chart/?asof=1991-02-12&view=releasedate&view2=domestic&yr=1990&sort=gross&order=DESC&p=.htm |archive-date=July 14, 2014 }}</ref>

===Critical reviews===
The show received a mixed reception from media publications. Some media outlets were more critical of the show. Rick DuBrow of the ''[[Los Angeles Times]]'' wrote, "It was a long day's journey into night for Oscar, one of the most effective sleeping pills of the year." He also added that while host Crystal started out strong, his jokes fell flat as the night progressed.<ref>{{cite news|last1=DuBrow |first1=Rick |title=Oscar Endures Another Hard Day's Night |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1991-03-26-ca-984-story.html |access-date=July 11, 2014 |work=Los Angeles Times |date=March 26, 1991 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140715010746/http://articles.latimes.com/1991-03-26/entertainment/ca-984_1_oscar-show |archive-date=July 15, 2014 }}</ref> ''[[The Washington Post]]'' television critic [[Tom Shales]] noted that Crystal, "followed many gags by instantly rating the reaction of the audience, as if it were up to them to please him instead of the other way around." In addition, he commented, "The Oscars seemed more of a fizzle than usual this year."<ref>{{cite news|last1=Shales|first1=Tom|title=The Show Doesn't Make A Spectacle of Itself|newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |date=March 27, 1991|page=B1}}</ref> Columnist Dan Craft of ''[[The Pantagraph]]'' remarked, "The Oscar show has become innocuously hip and yuppified. Kitsch and nostalgia have given way to efficiency and upward mobility. Everyone is tiresomely well-behaved and, worse, well-dressed." He also commented that host Crystal's insider showbiz jokes fell flat and were confusing to television audiences.<ref>{{cite news|title=New Academy Awards version isn't much fun|work=The Pantagraph|publisher=Lee Enterprises|date=March 29, 1991|page=C2}}</ref>

Other media outlets received the broadcast more positively. Columnist [[Harold Schindler]] of ''[[The Salt Lake Tribune]]'' wrote, "Billy Crystal kept things moving Monday night in such a manner that the extra quarter-hour was scarcely noticeable." He also said of the telecast's theme of film history, "The Academy used its film library to excellent advantage."<ref>{{cite news|last1=Schindler|first1=Harold|title=Academy Gives Its Best Performance As Crystal Sparkles on Oscar Night|work=The Salt Lake Tribune |date=March 27, 1991|page=A5}}</ref> Film critic [[Leonard Maltin]] remarked, "Emotions ran high and they gave us all a chance to feel vicariously what it might be like to win this kind of award...good guys finishing first and the part of Hollywood we like best, a happy ending."<ref name="Wiley 1996 812"/> ''[[Orlando Sentinel]]'' film critic Jay Boyar complimented Crystal for invigorating the gala, noting that his "clever remarks at the academy's 63rd annual awards presentation struck an entertaining balance between inside-Hollywood quips and general-audience jests."<ref>{{cite news|last1=Boyar |first1=Jay |title=Oscar Night's Improvements Are Crystal-clear |url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/1991/03/29/oscar-nights-improvements-are-crystal-clear/ |access-date=July 14, 2014 |work=Orlando Sentinel |date=March 29, 1991 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714225745/http://articles.orlandosentinel.com/1991-03-29/entertainment/9103280111_1_billy-crystal-sonny-bono-broadcast |archive-date=July 14, 2014 }}</ref>

===Ratings and reception===
The American telecast on ABC drew in an average of 42.7 million people over its length, which was a 6% increase from the [[62nd Academy Awards|previous year's ceremony]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Johnson |first=Greg |title=Call It the Glamour Bowl |url=https://articles.latimes.com/1999/mar/18/business/fi-18458/2 |access-date=August 26, 2013 |work=Los Angeles Times |date=March 18, 1999 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130928053918/http://articles.latimes.com/1999/mar/18/business/fi-18458/2 |archive-date=September 28, 2013 }}</ref> An estimated 76 million total viewers watched all or part of the awards.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Margulies |first1=Lee |title=TV Ratings: The Ratings Award Goes to Oscar |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1991-04-03-ca-1885-story.html |access-date=February 27, 2014 |work=Los Angeles Times |date=April 3, 1991 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140715044520/http://articles.latimes.com/1991-04-03/entertainment/ca-1885_1_ratings-award |archive-date=July 15, 2014 }}</ref> The show also drew higher [[Nielsen ratings]] compared to the previous ceremony, with 28.4% of households watching over a 48 share.<ref>{{cite news|last1=DuBrow |first1=Rick |title=Ratings Up Slightly for ABC's Oscar Telecast |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1991-03-27-ca-1084-story.html |access-date=July 11, 2014 |work=Los Angeles Times |date=March 27, 1991 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140715000350/http://articles.latimes.com/1991-03-27/entertainment/ca-1084_1_abc-s-oscar-telecast |archive-date=July 15, 2014 }}</ref> It was the most watched Oscars telecast since the [[56th Academy Awards|56th ceremony]] held in 1984.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Gorman |first1=Bill |title=1-Featured With No 'Avatar' Expect 'Academy Awards' Viewership To Fall; Ratings History + Your Guess For This Year (Poll) |url=http://tvbythenumbers.zap2it.com/2011/02/26/with-no-avatar-expect-academy-awards-viewership-to-fall-ratings-history-your-guess-for-this-year-poll/83754/ |access-date=February 28, 2014 |work=TV by the Numbers |publisher=Tribune Company |date=February 26, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714151329/http://tvbythenumbers.zap2it.com/2011/02/26/with-no-avatar-expect-academy-awards-viewership-to-fall-ratings-history-your-guess-for-this-year-poll/83754/ |archive-date=July 14, 2014 }}</ref>

In July 1991, the ceremony presentation received nine nominations at the [[43rd Primetime Emmy Awards|43rd Primetime Emmy]]s.<ref>{{cite news|title=Primetime Emmy Award database |url=http://www.emmys.com/shows/63rd-annual-academy-awards |access-date=July 11, 2014 |publisher=[[Academy of Television Arts and Sciences]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714204016/http://www.emmys.com/shows/63rd-annual-academy-awards |archive-date=July 14, 2014 }}</ref> The following month, the ceremony won three of those nominations for [[Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Variety Series|Outstanding Variety, Music, or Comedy Program]] (Gil Cates), [[Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Individual Performance in a Variety or Music Program|Outstanding Individual Performance in a Variety or Music Program]] (Billy Crystal), and [[Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Writing for a Variety Series|Outstanding Writing for a Variety or Music Program]] ([[Hal Kanter]], [[Buz Kohan]], Billy Crystal, [[David Steinberg]], [[Bruce Vilanch]], and [[Robert Wuhl]]).<ref>{{cite news|title=Emmy Awards: The Other Winners |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1991-08-26-ca-995-story.html |access-date=July 11, 2014 |work=Los Angeles Times |date=August 26, 1991 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714112217/http://articles.latimes.com/1991-08-26/entertainment/ca-995_1_academy-awards |archive-date=July 14, 2014 }}</ref>
